A given ray of light suffers minimum deviation in an equilateral prism P. Additional prisms Q and $R$ of identical shape and of same material as that of P are now combined as shown in figure. The ray will now suffer
solution: At minimum deviation the ray inside P is parallel to its base. As Q and R are identical and of the same material, the ray stays parallel to their bases, so the final deviation remains the same as before.

stem: A point charge $q_1 = 4q_0$ is placed at origin. Another point charge $q_2 = -q_0$ is placed at $x = 12$ cm. A proton of charge $q_0$ is placed on the x-axis such that the electrostatic force on the proton is zero. In this situation, the position of the proton from the origin is:
solution: Let the proton be at distance $x$ beyond $-q_0$. $\dfrac{q_0}{x^2} = \dfrac{4q_0}{(x+12)^2} \Rightarrow x + 12 = 2x \Rightarrow x = 12$. Distance from origin $= 24$ cm.

stem: There are two open organ pipes of the same length and the same material but of different radii. When they are emitting fundamental notes, which of the following is true?
options: broader pipe gives note of smaller frequency
both the pipes give notes of the same frequency
narrower pipe gives note of smaller frequency
either of them gives note of smaller or larger frequency depending on the wavelength of the wave.
solution: With end correction $e = 0.3r$: $f = \dfrac{v}{2(L + 2e)}$, so the broader pipe has the lower frequency.

A perfectly diamagnetic sphere has a small spherical cavity at its centre, which is filled with a paramagnetic substance. The whole system is placed in a uniform magnetic field $\vec B$. Then the field inside the paramagnetic substance is:
options: much larger than $|\vec B|$ and parallel to $\vec B$
much larger than $|\vec B|$ but opposite to $\vec B$
solution: A perfect diamagnet completely expels the magnetic field, so there is no field inside the cavity.
